Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 23 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Potion of Superheroism [5.5e]
fields.text:
When you drink this potion as a Bonus Action, you gain 30 temporary hit points that last for 1 hour. For the same duration, you are under the effect of a bless spell (no concentration required).

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 23 (Homebrew)

name: Purple Gem of the Vesve Forest [5.5e]

fields.name: Purple Gem of the Vesve Forest [5.5e]
fields.detail: very rare (requires attunement by an elf)
fields.text:
This magical gemstone is set in a silver bracelet and was originally created by elven wizards. As a Magic Action, you can spend one or more charges to cast one of the following spells:

Conjure animals (1 charge)
Conjure woodland beings (2 charges)
Conjure fey (3 charges)

When you spend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the gem becomes a blossoming flower.

	Recharge. The gem has 4 charges and recharges 1d4 spent charges daily at dawn.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 23 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Razor Claws of Chakyik [5.5e]
fields.text:
These magic claws were created by a wizard loyal to the Tiger Lord of the northwest. Each claw consists of four curved daggers attached to a leather gauntlet. When you wear these magic claws you can make an Unarmed Strike using Dexterity or Strength (your choice) and your proficiency bonus. The attack is magical. On a hit, you deal 4d4 slashing damage plus your Dexterity or Strength bonus.
	Additionally you have disadvantage on any Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, and you can't pick or hold any item.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 23 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Ring of Leadership [5.5e]
fields.text:
This silver ring is usually given to creatures in return to loyal friendship or unexpected favor. While wearing this magic ring, you have advantage on any Charisma while dealing with creatures Indifferent to you.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 23 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Ring of Stone [5.5e]
fields.text:
This golden ring contains a magic rock. As a Magic Action, you can spend one charge to cast the flesh to stone spell (Spell Save DC 17). The ring has 3 charges and cannot be recharged. When you spend the last charge, the ring becomes solid rock.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 24 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Rod of Electrification [5.5e]
fields.text:
This rod is made of a copper-nickel alloy. You gain a +1 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	On a successful hit, you can use a Bonus Action to deal an additional 1d8 Lightning damage.
	Once you use this property three times, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Sap (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Proficiency: simple, mace
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 24 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Rod of Entropy [5.5e]
fields.detail: mace, very rare (requires attunement by a creature of evil alignment)
fields.text:
This magic weapon is a short, blackened iron shaft topped by three skulls sculpted to look as though they have melted together.
	You gain a +2 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	As a Magic Action, you can create a 15-foot Emanation of a black aura. Each creature within the Emanation must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 3d6 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature must make the Constitution saving throw whenever the Emanation enters the creature's space, or whenever a creature enters the Emanation's space for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Proficiency: simple, mace
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 24 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Rod of Onwal [5.5e]
fields.detail: spellcasting focus, very rare (requires attunement by a creature of evil alignment)
fields.text:
This magic rod was originally crafted to protect the inhabitants of Onnwal against the fierce storms that regularly lash the Sea of Gearnat.
	While you are within a nonmagical storm that can potentially cause you one or more Hazards, you can use a Magic Action to calm the storm to a point that is no more dangerous.
	Once used this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 24 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Rod of the Aerdi Sea [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic rod was originally crafted for use by merchants who sail the pirate-infested waters between Hepmonaland and the Great Kingdom.
	As a Magic Action, you can spend one or more charges to cast one of the following spells (Spell Save DC 17):

	• fog cloud (1 charge)
	• hallucinatory terrain (2 charges)
	• programmed illusion (3 charges)

When you spend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the rod disappears.

	Recharge. The rod has 5 charges and recharges 1d4+1 spent charges daily at dawn.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Rod of the Wellwood [5.5e]
fields.text:
Fashioned from an oaken branch, this magic rod was originally crafted by druids who inhabited the majestic forest of Welkwood.
	While you hold this magic rod in your hand, you gain the following benefits:

	• You can use the rod as a magical staff +1. You are proficient in this weapon.

	• As a Magic Action, you can spend one or more charges to cast one of the following spells (Spell Save DC 17): entangle (1 charge), plant growth (2 charges), wall of thorns (3 charges)

When you spend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the rod disappears.

	Recharge. The rod has 5 charges and recharges 1d4+1 spent charges daily at dawn.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Scant Wand of Storms [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic wand was originally created in the capital city of Onnwal, and has been used against raiding warships from the South Province. Its first creator was undoubtedly influenced by observing the furious weather in the Sea of Gearnat.
	While you hold this magic wand, you can use a Magic Action to create a 30–foot radius Sphere centered on a point that you can see within range. Since that area is filled by heavy rain and lightning, it's Lightly Obscured and is a Difficult Terrain. When a creature that starts its turn there or enters the Sphere for the first time on a turn, it must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 8d8 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage and no other ill effects on a successful one.
	The Sphere lasts for 1 minute or earlier if you dismiss it with a Bonus Action. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Scroll of the Death Servant [5.5e]
fields.text:
This scroll reads "For you, the greatest gift of all".
	When you read this scroll, the scroll crumbles to dust and you feel a chill and then a warmth drifts across your back. A death servant has merged into your shadow. The first time you are about to die, the death servant dies instead of you, dissipating in a cloud of black vapor.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Scroll of the Efreeti [5.5e]
fields.text:
Upon this magic scroll there are many flaming runes and sigils. While you carry this magic scroll you have Resistance to Fire damage. As a Magic Action, you can read the scroll and cast the conjure elemental spell (only Fire Elemental). Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Silver Key of Portals [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic item is a regular-sized silver skeleton key. As a Utilize Action, you can place the skeleton key on any locked door (either magically or not), immediately unlocking the door. Once you use this property twice, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 26 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Skull-Staff of Hepmonaland [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic staff is a 7-foot-long pole topped with a skull with a wild mane of white hair and sharp, demonic features.
	You gain a +1 bonus to your AC while you hold that staff. Additionally, you can use a Magic Action to force a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you to look at the school. The target must succeed on a Wisdom DC 15 saving throw or has the Frightened condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its next turns, the target can make another Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
	Once you use this property twice, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 26 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Spider's Boots of Stealth [5.5e]
fields.text:
Spider was the nickname of the premier thief of the city of Rel Astra. No one knew anything else about him. Spider was a loner elf who never formed a close relationship with anyone in the Rel Astran Thieves' Guild.
	These magic boots are black, calf-length suede boots with a criss crossing pattern of silver webs. While you wear these magic boots, you gain the following effects:

	• You can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

	• You ignore movement restrictions caused by webbing.

	• You are immune to any effect caused by webbing.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 26 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Staff of Hornwood [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic staff was originally created by a wizard who wanted to make her travel in the wilderness less dangerous.
	As a Magic Action, you create a 10-foot Emanation from you. This Emanation prevents any creature with an Intelligence score of 4 from passing or reaching through it. If you move and the Emanation enters the space of one of such creatures, that creature must use its Reaction to move away from the Emanation's area.
	The Emanation lasts for 1 hour or earlier if you dismiss it as a Bonus Action. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 27 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Staff of Celene [5.5e]
fields.text:
Set on a silver necklace, this golden medallion is usually given as a gift to those who performed great services for high elves in Celene.
	When you openly wear this magic necklace, you have Advantage on any Influence Action against elves.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 27 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Starburst Insignia [5.5e]
fields.detail: rare (requires attunement by a cleric or paladin of good alignment)
fields.text:
This insignia has rubies embedded with them and were created by the church of St. Cuthbert.
	When you wear this magic item around your neck you have advantage on any Wisdom saving throw and ability check.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 27 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Stonefist [5.5e]
fields.detail: greatsword, very rare (requires attunement by a fighter)
fields.text:
This magic greatsword is also known as the Sword of Rage, and was enchanted during the reign of Vlek Col Vlekzed. You gain a +2 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Additionally, when you make an attack with this magic weapon, you can choose to have advantage on that attack. If you choose so, however, attacks made against you have advantage until the start of your next turn.

Proficiency: martial, greatsword
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 27 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Sulward's Axe [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic axe is magically sharpened to aid woodsmen in cutting rare woods to be exported from the Lordship of the Isles. You gain a +1 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and if the target is a Plant the bonus becomes +2. Additionally, you gain advantage on any Wisdom (Survival) check.

Topple (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

Versatile: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Proficiency: martial, battleaxe
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 28 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Symbol of True Death [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic item is a small amulet that looks like a red skull, usually carved from bone, in front of a circular fan of fire made of steel but plated in gold.
	While you wear this magic amulet, you have advantage on any Death saving throw.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 28 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Thillonrian Shield [5.5e]
fields.text:
While you hold this magic shield, you gain a +2 bonus on your AC. This magic shield helps you to inspire your allies. As a Magic Action, each creature Allied to you within 120 feet that can hear you has advantage on any saving throw against the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned condition.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 28 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Timeglass of the Wizard [5.5e]
fields.detail: very rare (requires attunement by a wizard)
fields.text:
This magic item appears to be a 1-foot-tall hourglass. As a Magic Action, you can spend two or more charges to cast on the following spells (Spell Save DC17):

	• haste (2 charges)
	• slow (2 charge)
	• time stop (3 charges)

When you spend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the hourglass disappears.

	Recharge. The hourglass has 3 charges and recharges 1d2 charges daily at dawn.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 28 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Tiger Cloak of Chalyik [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic cloak is fashioned from the complete hide of an adult tiger. It includes head, skin, and claws, dangling at the sides.
	When you wear this magic cloak, you gain the ability to enter in Rage, as the Barbarian class, as a Magic Action. If you have a level in the Barbarian class, then you have one more use of this ability.
	Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 28 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Trident of the Oljatt Sea [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic weapon is rumored to be a weapon of sahuagin fighters. You gain a +2 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	As a Magic Action, you can unleash a jet of steam that forms a Line 60-foot-long and 10-foot-wide originating from the trident.
	Each creature in the Line makes a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 6d8 Force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
	Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Proficiency: simple, trident
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 28 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Tusmit Battle's Crescent [5.5e]
fields.detail: trident, uncommon (requires attunement by a barbarian, fighter, paladin, or ranger)
fields.text:
Set in a golden necklace studded with gems, this magic medallion is a prized possession among warriors.
	As a Bonus Action, you have advantage on all your weapon attacks for 1 minute. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 28 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Wand of Force [5.5e]
fields.text:
While you hold this magic wand, you gain the following benefits.

	• As a Magic Action, you can create a 60-foot long and 5-foot wide Line that originates from the tip of the wand. Each creature in the Line must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once you use this property twice, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

	• As a Magic Action, you can cast the wall of force spell(Spell Save DC17). Once you cast this spell, you can't cast it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 29 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Wand of Highfolk [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic wand was originally created by high elves in the northwest.
	While you hold this magic wand, you can use a Magic Action to target up to 6 creatures that are allies with each other. Each target makes a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Charmed condition and becomes Hostile to the other targets and sees them as Hostile. The condition lasts for 1 minute. At the end of each of its next turns, an affected creature can make another Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 29 (Homebrew)

name: Wand of Secret Door & Trap Detection [5.5e]

fields.name: Wand of Secret Door & Trap Detection [5.5e]
fields.text:
As a Magic Action, while you hold this magic wand, you can find any secret door or trap within 120 feet of you. Once you use this property twice, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 29 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Werebane [5.5e]
fields.text:
You have a +1 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	When you successfully hit a Shapechanger, you deal additional 2d12 damage.

Nick (Mastery): When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action in· stead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

Finesse: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

Light: When you take the Attack action on your turn and. attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

Thrown: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

Range: A weapon that can be used to make a ranged attack has a range shown in parentheses after the ammunition or thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second indicates the weapon's maximum range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the weapon's long range.

Proficiency: simple, dagger
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 29 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Whip of Zeif [5.5e]
fields.text:
You have a +2 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. As a Magic Action, you can crack the whip in the air. Each creature within 120 feet that can hear the crack must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or has the Deafened condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its next turns, an affected creature can make another Constitution saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
	Once you use this property twice, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Slow (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

Finesse: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

Reach: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

Proficiency: simple, whip
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 29 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Whistle of Axewood [5.5e]
fields.text:
This silver instrument was originally created by elven wizards to deal with Fey.
	When you play this magic instrument as a Bonus Action, you gain advantage on any Influence Action made while dealing with Fey.
	Once you use this property twice, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 29 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Whiteshiver Elixir [5.5e]
fields.text:
This small glass vial contains a thick, milky elixir with a foul smell reminiscent of rotting mushrooms.
	When you drink this magic potion as a Bonus Action, you gain the following benefits for 1 hour.

	• You are a Plant. You maintain your Humanoid Type.

	• You have Resistance to Poison damage and you are Immune to the Poisoned condition.

	• You have Darkvision 120 feet.

	• As a Magic Action, you can release spores in a 30foot Sphere centered on you. Each creature within the Sphere must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 Poison Damage and having the Poisoned condition for 1 minute on a failed save, or half as much damage and no other ill effects on a successful one. An affected creature must make another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its next turns, ending the effect on itself on a successful save, Once you use this property twice, you can't use it again.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 29 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Wings of the Rakers [5.5e]
fields.text:
This white cloak was originally enchanted by a wizard who found a welcome home among the Griff Mountains and the Rakers.
	While you wear this magic cloak, as a Bonus Action the cloak takes the appearance of white seagull wings and you gain Fly Speed 30 feet. Additionally, when you are flying and you dive at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hit it with a melee weapon attack, you deal an extra 2d8 damage to the target. The white seagull wings disappear after 1 hour or earlier if you dismiss them as a Bonus Action. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 30 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Wizard's Robe [5.5e]
fields.text:
While you wear this magic robe, you can spend one or more charges to cast one of the following spells (Spell Save DC 15):

	• charm person (1 charge)
	• hold person (2 charges)
	• charm monster (3 charges)
	• hold monster (4 charges)
	• polymorph (4 charges)

When you spend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the robe crumbles to dust.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 30 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Wolf Cloak of Wegwiur [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magical cloak is made from the hide of a winter wolf, and includes a wolf's head, pelt, claws, and tail. Originally, it was enchanted by priests of the Wolf Nomads.
	When you wear this magic cloak, you gain the following benefits.

	• You have Resistance to Cold damage.

	• As a Magic Action, you can have advantage on any Wisdom and Dexterity Test for 1 minute. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 30 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Woodworker's Tools of Dyvers [5.5e]
fields.text:
Ability: Dexterity
Utilize: Carve a pattern in wood (DC 10)
Craft: Club, Greatclub, Quarterstaff, Ranged weapons (except Pistol, Musket, and  Sling), Arcane Focus, Arrows, Bolts, Druidic Focus, Ink Pen, Needles

This magical set of Woodcarver's Tools was originally enchanted for a carpenter in the City of Dyvers. You are proficient in this magical set of Woodcarver's Tools and when you use them, you have advantage on any check roll.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 30 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Zazyg's Spell Component Pouch
fields.detail: rare (requires attunement by a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard)
fields.text:
This item is a normal belt pouch of unremarkable sort. The famous archmage Zazyg is rumored to be the first crafter of this magic item. When you wear this magic pouch and you are casting a spell you pick from the pouch a desired material spell component of a value up to 100 gp. The component always disappears after you cast the spell.
	Once used this property three times, you must finish a Long Rest before you can use it again.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 30 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Black Crown of Aerdy [5.5e]
fields.text:
This evil headgear was worn by one of the first Overkings of House Naelax in the ancient Great Kingdom. Whether the crown was enchanted by an evil wizard or whether it merely became a receptacle for the Overking's cruel spirit is not known. The powers of the crown exist only to recreate the greatness and wickedness of that Overking.
	When you attune to this magic item by donning it, your Intelligence and Wisdom score raise by 4 up to a maximum of 24, and you gain one Epic Boon of your choice, even if your level is lower than 19, and your alignment becomes lawful evil.
	Each time you finish a Long Rest you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save your Constitution score permanently lowers by 1. When your Constitution score becomes 0, you die and become a specter guarding the crown.
	After the attunement to this magic item, donning it, you don't voluntarily remove it.
	The crown can be removed only by a wish spell.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 32 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Blade of Chaos [5.5e]
fields.text:
The blade of this iron longsword is laced with thin lines of mithral that seem to shift and move constantly. Two twisted pieces of silver that end in large emeralds serve as its quillons. The handle is wrapped in green leather, and the pommel consists of a third emerald set into silver talons.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It has the following additional properties.

	Binding Strike: When you successfully hit a creature with a melee attack, the target must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or has the Paralyzed condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its next turns, an affected creature can make another Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
	On a successful save, target creature is immune to this effect for the next 24 hours. Spells: as a Magic Action, you can cast the darkness and the ray of enfeeblement spell (Spell Save DC 17). Once you cast one of those spells, you can't cast that spell again until you finish a Long Rest.

	Sentience: Blade of Chaos is a sentient chaotic neutral weapon with an Intelligence of 17, a Wisdom of 10, and a Charisma of 17. It has hearing and Darkvision out of a range of 120 feet. The weapon can speak, read, and understand Common, and can communicate with its wielder telepathically. Its voice is arrogant and harsh. While you are attuned to it, Blade of Chaos also understands every language you know.

	Personality: Blade of Chaos speaks with an arrogant voice, expecting to be obeyed and considering its wielders as inferior beings. The weapon's purpose is to add unpredictability to any situation while avoiding the boundaries of rules and laws.

Proficiency: simple, longsword
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 32 (Homebrew)

name: Blue Armor of the Crystalmist Mountains [5.5e]

fields.name: Blue Armor of the Crystalmist Mountains [5.5e]
fields.text:
This scale armor is cut from the hide of adult or ancient blue dragons and it is crafted by the mountain dwarves of the Cystalmist range. While you wear this magic scale armor you gain the following benefits.

	• You gain a +3 bonus to your AC.

	• You gain Resistance to Lightning damage.

The wearer has disadvantage on Stealth (Dexterity) checks.

Proficiency: medium armor
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 33 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Chalice of the Shield Lands [5.5e]
fields.detail: legendary (requires attunement by a creature of good alignment who is not a paladin)
fields.text:
This golden chalice was enchanted in response to the growing menace of the Horned Society.
	When you drink as a Magic Action from this chalice, you can gain the abilities of a Paladin of Devotion of the same level as you (Minimum level 3) for 1 hour. You retain all the abilities of your class.
	Once you use this property, you can't use it again until 7 days have passed.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 33 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Dreamsinger [5.5e]
fields.detail: rapier, legendary (requires attunement by a bard)
fields.text:
Dreamsinger is one of the Five Blades of Corusk. It has a blade of white steel and is set with moonstones.
	When you are not attuned to it, you gain a +1 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

	• When you are attuned to it, you gain the following benefits.

	• You gain a +3 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

	• You have a +2 bonus to your AC and to any saving throw.

	• You can sense automatically the exact position of another Blade of Corusk as long as it is within 1 mile of you.

Vex (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

Finesse: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

Proficiency: martial, rapier
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 34 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Equalizer of Gran March [5.5e]
fields.detail: longsword, legendary (requires attunement by a creature of neutral alignment)
fields.text:
This silver longsword was created to be a tool for the balancing powers of the Multiverse. While you hold this magic weapon, you have a +3 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	When you successfully hit a creature of a non-neutral alignment or that's not unaligned, you can use a Bonus Action to invoke the balancing powers. The target must succeed on DC 19 Charisma saving throw or it is completely disintegrated. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Sap (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Versatile: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Proficiency: simple, longsword
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 34 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Fire Wand of the Sueloise [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic wand may have been the device that caused the destruction of the Suel Empire.
	While you hold this magic wand, you can use a Magic Action to spend 3 charges and create a 60-foot Cube to a point that you can see within 120 feet of you. The Cube contains a rain of magical fire that burns everyone and everything. Each creature within the Cube must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 12d8 Fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On each of your next turns, you can spend a Bonus Action to maintain the Cube, and each creature that starts its turn there or enters the Cube for the first time on a turn must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 12d8 Fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Objects not carried or worn within the cube other than those made of mithral and adamantine take 12d8 Fire damage at the end of each of your turns as long as the Cube lasts.
	When you spend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 10 or lower, the wand explodes in a Sphere of 60-foot radius centered on you. Each creature within the sphere must make a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 24d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

	Recharge. The wand has 6 charges and recharges 1d6 spent charges daily at dawn.

Proficiency: simple, wand
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 34 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Greenswathe [5.5e]
fields.detail: scimitar, legendary (requires attunement by a druid)
fields.text:
Greenswathe is one of the Five Blades of Corusk. It is made of a gold-colored alloy as hard as adamantine. When you are not attuned to it, you gain a +1 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	When you are attuned to it, you gain a +3 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Additionally, when you successfully hit a target with this magic weapon, as a Bonus Action you deal 2d6 additional damage. Once you use this property three times, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Nick (Mastery): When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action in· stead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

Finesse: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

Light: When you take the Attack action on your turn and. attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

Proficiency: martial, scimitar
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 36 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215

fields.name: Harmonizer [5.5e]
fields.detail: shortsword, legendary (requires attunement by a rogue)
fields.text:
Harmonizer is one of the Five Blades of Corusk. Across the shiny surface of this magic weapon are etched images of a wizard performing a ritual over five swords. You gain a +3 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	When you attune to this magic item, the sword creates a clone of you and each creature Allied to you within 120 feet of you. The clones are Fey, appear in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you and they are Hostile to you and your allies.

Vex (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

Finesse: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

Light: When you take the Attack action on your turn and. attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

Proficiency: martial, shortsword
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 36 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215

fields.name: Horn of the Azure Sea [5.5e]
fields.detail: legendary (requires attunement by a creature of evil alignment)
fields.text:
This magic horn was originally created by an evil cleric. This magic item functions only at night on the open sea.
	As a Magic Action, you can blow the horn and a Huge ghost ship appears in an unoccupied space on the sea within 360 feet of you. Each creature other than you and your allies that can see that ghost ship must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or has the Frightened condition for 1 minute. The ghost ship disappears after 1 minute or earlier if you dismiss it as a Bonus Action. When the ship disappears, the condition ends on the affected creatures.
	Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 37 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215

name: Iron Crown of the Bandit Kingdom [5.5e]

fields.name: Iron Crown of the Bandit Kingdom [5.5e]
fields.text:
This metal headgear was fashioned for fighters. When you wear this magic crown, you have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened condition.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 37 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215

fields.name: Mace of St. Cuthbert [5.5e]
fields.detail: mace, legendary (requires attunement by a cleric or paladin of a lawful good alignment)
fields.text:
This magic mace is known to be a relic created by St.Cuthbert himself. You gain a +3 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	When you hit a Fiend or an Undead with this magic weapon, that creature takes an extra 2d6 radiant damage. If the target has 25 hit points or fewer, it must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be destroyed. On a successful save, that creature has the Frightened condition until the end of your next turn. While you hold this weapon, it sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius, and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet.
	As a Magic Action, you can spend one or more charges to cast one of the following spells:

	• bless (1 charge)
	• remove curse (2 charge)
	• heal (3 charges)
	• resurrection (5 charges)

When you spend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, your Intelligence score lowers by 1. If your Intelligence score reaches 3 in such a manner, you become an NPC Celestial servant of St.Cuthbert.

	Recharge. This magic mace has 5 charges and recharges 1d4+1 spent charges daily at dawn

Sap (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Proficiency: simple, mace
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 37 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215

fields.name: Prism of Greyhawk [5.5e]
fields.detail: legendary (requires attunement by a bard, sorcerer, or wizard)
fields.text:
This crystal tool was originally enchanted to enhance the prism's ability to create dazzling colors.
	As a Magic Action, you can cast the prismatic ray or the prismatic wall spells(Spell Save DC 19). Once you cast one of these two spells, you can't use this property again until you finish a Long Rest.
	This magic item functions only if you are in sunlight.

Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 37 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215

fields.name: Red Armor of the Hellfurnaces [5.5e]
fields.text:
This scale armor was cut from the back plates of adult or ancient red dragons. Many warriors from the Yeomanry died in battle to kill those creatures, and the best armorers were hired to rework the plates into a wearable armor. While wearing this magic scale armor you gain the following benefits.

	• You gain a +3 bonus to your AC.
	• You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

The wearer has disadvantage on Stealth (Dexterity) checks.

Proficiency: medium armor
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 38 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 219

fields.name: Scepter of the Forgotten City [5.5e]
fields.detail: scale mail, legendary (requires attunement by a cleric or wizard)
fields.text:
A relic of a lost civilization, this wandlike scepter is a 2-foot-long shaft of silver with a large red gem at the tip. It was used by some of the original lords of the Suel Empire; when that kingdom was turned into the Sea of Dust, the wand was lost. A recent expedition from the Yeomanry rediscovered the wand, and those explorers claimed that it came from the Forgotten City itself. Whether or not that claim is true, the scepter certainly contains some of the greatness that built the lost empire, and much of the madness that destroyed it.
	As a Magic Action, you can spend one charge to raise your Intelligence and Wisdom scores to 25 for the next 24 hours. Each time you spend one charge, you must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, your Constitution score lowers by 1. When your Constitution reaches 0, you die and your corpse raises as a wraith in the next 24 hours.
	When you spend the last charge, the scepter disappears.

	Recharge. The Scepter has 25 charges and cannot be recharged.

Proficiency: simple, rod
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 38 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Shield of Greyhawk [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic shield bears Greyhawk's coat of arms and was originally created by the Society of the Magi. It now hangs in the audience hall of the Lord Mayor's mansion.
	While you hold this magic shield, you gain the following benefits.

	• You gain a +3 bonus to your AC.

	• You can cast the dispel evil and good spell. Once you use this property twice, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Utilize Action to Don or Doff.

Proficiency: shield
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 38 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 219

fields.name: Silver Crown of Veluna [5.5e]
fields.detail: shield, legendary (requires attunement by a cleric of good alignment)
fields.text:
Encrusted with small green gems, this silver crown recently appeared among the ruling clerics of Veluna. The Canon himself has often worn it, though he may sometimes loan it to trusted agents of Veluna when they embark on important, holy missions.
	While you wear this magic item, you gain the following benefits.

	• Your Wisdom score increases by 2 up to a maximum of 22.
	• You are under the permanent effect of a protection from good and evil spell, but you are protected only by Aberrations, Elementals, Fiends, and Undead.

Proficiency: shield
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 40 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Soul Gem [5.5e]
fields.text:
This glowing magic gem floats in the air, slowly rotating around you. As a Magic Action, you can spend 1 charge and the gem makes a blast of negative energy towards a creature that you can see within 60 feet. The target must make a DC 21 Constitution saving throw, taking 10d10 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If the target reaches 0 hp, it immediately dies, its soul is entrapped within the gem, and it can't be resurrected, unless the gem is broken. This magic gem has AC 20, 50 hit points, and has Immunity to Poison, Necrotic, Psychic damage, and to Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage made with non magical attacks.
	Each time you spend a charge, you consume a soul trapped within the gem. The DM chooses which soul is consumed. If its soul is consumed, that creature can be resurrected only by a wish spell.

	Recharge. This magic gem recharges 1 charge each time a soul is trapped within.

Proficiency: shield
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 40 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Stalker [5.5e]
fields.detail: longsword, legendary (requires attunement by a ranger)
fields.text:
Stalker is a one of the Five Blades of Corusk. It is a longsword with a blue steel blade and a hilt, pommel, and crosspiece of black adamantine. Wisps of shadowstuff seem to move silently across its surface.
	When you are not attuned to it, you gain a +1 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	When you are attuned to it, you gain a +3 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and you gain advantage on any Dexterity (Stealth) and Wisdom (Survival) check.

Sap (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Versatile: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Proficiency: martial, longsword
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 41 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215

fields.name: Sword of Azor'alq [5.5e]
fields.text:
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It has the following additional properties.

	Crush Evil: When you successfully hit an Aberration or a Fiend, the target must succeed on DC 19 Constitution saving throw or it is disintegrated. Once you successfully use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

	Detect Evil: As a Magic Action, you can exactly locate any Aberration or Fiend within 1 mile of you. When you use this property three times, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

	Spells: As a Magic Action, you can cast the fly spell. Once you cast this spell, you can't cast it again until you finish a Long Rest.

	Sentience: The Sword of Azor'alq is a sentient neutral good weapon with an Intelligence of 17, a Wisdom of 10, and a Charisma of 16. It has hearing and Darkvision out of a range of 120 feet. The weapon can speak, read, and understand Common and Elvish, and can communicate with its wielder telepathically. Its voice is proud and noble. While you are attuned to it, the weapon also understands every language you know.

	Personality: The Sword of Azor'alq is very proud and does not wish to serve anyone who is not an important baron or king. It also expect its owner to provide it with a new scabbard, with gems fixed to it. In general, the sword thinks it is in charge of any owner. The sword especially hates Fiends and Aberrations and actively seeks out to destroy them.

Sap (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Versatile: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Proficiency: martial, longsword
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 41 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215

fields.name: Talisman of Zagy [5.5e]
fields.text:
This magic item is an oddly-shaped bit of extrusive rock, shaped and roughly polished.
	When you attune to this magic item, roll a d20. On a 10 or lower, this magic item gives you a Curse. As long as you have that Curse, your Speed is halved and you have Disadvantage on any Strength Test.
	The Curse can be removed by a greater restoration spell or greater magic. On a 11 or higher, this magic item grants you the ability to cast the wish spell as a Magic Action.
	Once you cast the spell, the talisman disappears.

Proficiency: martial, longsword
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 41 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215

fields.name: The Edge [5.5e]
fields.detail: bastard sword, legendary (requires attunement by a fighter)
fields.text:
The Edge is one of the Five Blades of Corusk. This magic weapon is a bastard sword whose blade is made of graysh steel. The hilt of the sword is covered in soft suede leather. Jutting from the pommel, three blackened daggers point outward like venomous fango.
	You gain a +3 bonus to your attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
	As a Magic Action, you can order the three blackened daggers to fly and hit a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. You can direct the daggers to one or more targets. For each time that is hit by a dagger, the target must make on a DC 19 Constitution saving throw, taking 4d10 Poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
	Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Sap (Mastery): If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Versatile: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

Proficiency: martial, bastard sword
Source:	Treasures from Oerth p. 41 (Homebrew),
		Player's Handbook (2024) p. 215
